=== FILE: Are Bands a Bad Idea for Rotator Cuff Strengthening？ ｜ elitefts.com [iNqKLSLRMfQ].txt ===

It's going on guys. Jordan Schallel here with the lead FTS. Just wanted to recap an article I wrote about using bands to strengthen the rotator cuff. Now, common practice we see in gyms a lot. It's a little bit better than describing plates and flopping your arms around, but it's something that you might want to think about reconsidering as putting as part of your warm-up. Now, every muscle has a strength curve. An ability to exert force across different lengths of the muscle. More often than not muscles are weak when it's fully lengthened and muscles are weak when they're fully short. Like a bicep isn't really strong. Here, nor is a bicep really stronGHere. It's kind of strong right in that middle part of that curve. So if we think of fully lengthened, fully short and most muscles operate from this, what's called that length tension relationship. Muscles of the rotator cuff are no different. So if we think about now the resistance profile, which is how this band is going to exert force against our rotator cuff, this band is going to get harder. It's going to exert more force as we approach that fully short and position of the muscles that externally rotate our shoulder. In this case, predominantly a muscle called your infraspinatus. This is one of your rotator cuff muscles. So if we think muscles are weak when they're short, we don't want resistance that increases into the position in where muscle gets weak. So if that infraspinatus is weakest as we externally rotate to that fully short and position, we don't then want to add resistance through that plane that's getting increasingly more difficult to overcome as our ability to overcome drops off. So rather than using a band to strengthen your rotator cuff, perhaps using an implement like a cable set up in a very similar way, we're just going to have a uniform distribution of force across that that strength curve of the muscles we're trying to tren might be a better adaptation to put into our trening to help build those muscles of stability around the shoulder.
